Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 48, verses 1–7 (part 1 of 2):

It is Madani (revealed in Medina). Al-Qurtubi said: by consensus.

Ibn al-Durays, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Surat al-Fath was revealed in Medina."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr something similar.

Ibn Ishaq and al-Hakim narrated, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il authenticated it, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan, who both said: "Surat al-Fath was revealed between Mecca and Medina, concerning the affair of al-Hudaybiyah, from its beginning to its end." This does not contradict the consensus that it is Madani, because what is meant by a Madani surah is one revealed after the Hijrah from Mecca.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited Surat al-Fath on his riding beast during his journey in the year of the Conquest, and he repeated it."

In the two Sahihs, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was traveling on some of his journeys, and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was traveling with him at night. 'Umar asked him about something, but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not answer him. Then he asked him again, and he did not answer him. Then he asked him again, and he did not answer him. So 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: 'May the mother of 'Umar be bereaved! I pressed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) three times, and each time he did not answer you.' 'Umar said: 'So I urged my camel forward, and went ahead of the people, and I feared that some Qur'an might be revealed concerning me. I had not waited long when I heard a crier calling me, so I said: I greatly fear that some Qur'an has been revealed concerning me. So I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and greeted him, and he said: "Indeed, a surah has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than everything the sun rises upon," then he recited: ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory﴾" [i.e., Surat al-Fath].

In Sahih Muslim, from Qatadah, that Anas ibn Malik related to them: "When there was revealed ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory﴾, up to His saying: ﴿a great triumph﴾ [al-Fath 48:1], upon his return from al-Hudaybiyah, while they were mixed with sorrow and grief, and they had slaughtered the sacrificial animals at al-Hudaybiyah, he said: 'Indeed there has been revealed to me a verse that is dearer to me than the whole world.'"

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory﴾ — scholars differed about the identification of this victory (fath). The majority said: it is the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, and a treaty may be called a victory (fath).

Al-Farra' said: "Fath may be a treaty. The linguistic meaning of fath (opening) is the opening of what is closed, and the treaty that was with the polytheists at al-Hudaybiyah was blocked and impossible until Allah opened it."

Al-Zuhri said: "There was no victory greater than the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, because the polytheists mixed with the Muslims and heard their speech, so Islam took firm root in their hearts, and in three years a great number embraced Islam, and the number of Muslims increased through them."

Al-Sha'bi said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gained at al-Hudaybiyah what he had not gained in any military campaign: Allah forgave him what came before of his sin and what came after, he received the Pledge of Ridwan, they were fed from the palm-groves of Khaybar, the offering reached its place of sacrifice, and the Romans prevailed over the Persians, so the believers rejoiced at the victory of the People of the Book over the Magians."

Others said: it is the Conquest of Mecca.

Others said: it is the Conquest of Khaybar.

The first view is more preferred, and what we mentioned earlier supports it, namely that the surah was revealed concerning al-Hudaybiyah.

It has also been said: it is all the conquests that Allah granted to His Messenger. It has been said: it is what He opened for him of prophethood and the call to Islam. It has been said: it is the conquest of Rome. It has been said: what is meant by fath in this verse is judgment and decision, as in His saying: ﴿Decide between us and our people with truth﴾ [al-A'raf 7:89]. So it is as if He said: "Indeed We have decided for you a clear decision," meaning evident, plain, and manifest.

﴿That Allah may forgive you your past sins and those to come﴾ — the lam is connected to (fatahna), and it is the lam of causation (lam al-'illah).

Ibn al-Anbari said: "I asked Abu al-'Abbas, meaning al-Mubarrad, about the lam in His saying ﴿That Allah may forgive you﴾, and he said: it is the lam of kay, its meaning being: 'Indeed We have granted you a clear victory so that there may be gathered for you, along with forgiveness, the completion of blessing in the victory. When something occurring and contingent is joined to forgiveness, the meaning of kay becomes fitting.' Whoever said that the victory is not the cause of forgiveness erred."

The author of al-Kashshaf said: the lam was not a cause of forgiveness, but rather of the gathering of the four matters enumerated, namely: forgiveness, the completion of blessing, guidance to the straight path, and mighty victory.

As if it were said: "We made easy for you the conquest of Mecca and gave you victory over your enemy, so that We might gather for you the honor of both abodes and the benefits of the immediate and the deferred."

This is not a good statement, for the lam governs forgiveness, so it is the cause of the victory; how then can it be a cause of something else?

Al-Razi, in explaining the causal reading, said: what is meant by His saying ﴿That Allah may forgive you﴾ is the making known of forgiveness; its implied sense is: "We have granted you victory so that you may know that you are forgiven and protected from sin."

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: what is meant is that Allah granted you victory so that the victory would be a sign of His forgiveness of you, so it is as if it were the lam of becoming (lam al-sayrurah).

Abu Hatim said: it is the lam of oath, and this is an error, for the lam of oath is not given a kasra and does not govern a mansub (accusative) noun.

There is difference concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿what came before of your sin and what came after﴾. It has been said: what came before of your sin is that before prophethood, and what came after is that after it; this was said by Mujahid, Sufyan al-Thawri, Ibn Jarir, al-Wahidi, and others.

'Ata' said: "What came before of your sin" means the sin of your two parents, Adam and Hawwa'; and what came after is the sins of your community. How far this is from the meaning of the Qur'an!

It has been said: what came before is the sin of your father Ibrahim, and what came after is the sins of the prophets after him. This is like the preceding view in its remoteness.

It has been said: what came before is the sin (p-1381) of the Day of Badr, and what came after is the sin of the Day of Hunayn. This is like the first two views in its remoteness.

It has been said: "Had there been a sin, old or new, We would have forgiven it for you." Other views were stated that have no basis, and the first is the most appropriate.

The meaning of "sin" after prophethood may be the leaving of what is better, and it is called a sin concerning him because of the greatness of his rank, even though it is not a sin in regard to others.

﴿And complete His blessing upon you﴾ — by making your religion manifest over all religion. It has been said: by Paradise; it has been said: by prophethood and wisdom; it has been said: by the conquest of Mecca, al-Ta'if, and Khaybar. The preferable meaning is: that there may be gathered for you, along with the victory, the completion of blessing through forgiveness and guidance to a straight path, which is Islam. The meaning of "yahdika" (guide you) is: He keeps you firm upon guidance until He takes you to Himself.

﴿And that Allah may aid you with a mighty aid﴾ — that is, a victorious, unassailable aid that is not followed by humiliation.

﴿It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers﴾ — that is, calm and serenity, through the victory He made easy for them, so that their souls would not be disturbed by what befalls them, ﴿that they may increase in faith along with their faith﴾ — that is, that they may increase, by means of that tranquility, in faith added to the faith they already had before.

al-Kalbi said: "Whenever a verse descended from the sky and they affirmed it, their affirmation increased upon their affirmation." al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "fear along with their fear." al-Dahhak said: "certainty along with their certainty."

﴿And to Allah belong the armies of the heavens and the earth﴾ — meaning the angels, mankind, jinn, and devils; He manages their affairs as He wills, empowers some of them over others, and surrounds some of them by others. And Allah is ever Knowing, abundantly knowledgeable, Wise in His acts and sayings.

﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ — this lam is connected to an omitted element indicated by what precedes it; its implied sense: "He tests with those armies whom He wills, so He accepts good from its people and evil from whomever He has decreed it for, in order that He may admit and punish." It has been said: it is connected to "Indeed We have granted you a victory," as if He said: "Indeed We have granted you what We have granted, so that He may admit and punish." It has been said: it is connected to "yansurak" (aid you): that is, Allah aided you through the believers so that He may admit and punish. It has been said: it is connected to "yazdaadu" (increase): that they may increase so that He may admit and punish. The first is the most preferable.

﴿And remove from them their misdeeds﴾ — that is, He covers them, does not expose them, and does not punish them for them. He placed admission before expiation, although the matter is the reverse, in order to hasten to the statement of what is the highest aim and the most sublime purpose. ﴿And that is with Allah a great triumph﴾ — that is, success in attaining every desire, deliverance from every distress, attraction of every benefit, and repelling of every harm. His saying "with Allah" (indeed 'Inda Allah) is connected to an omitted element, being a circumstantial clause (hal) from "fawzan" (triumph), because it was originally an attribute; when it was placed first it became a circumstance: that is, "existing with Allah." The sentence is parenthetical, placed between the reward of the believers and the reward of the hypocrites and polytheists.

Then, having finished what He promised to His righteous servants, He mentioned what others deserve, saying: 6 — ﴿And He punishes the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women﴾ — this is coordinated with (yudkhila), that is: He punishes them in this world with the worries and griefs that reach them because of what they witness of the elevation of the word of Islam and the subjugation of its opponents, and with what they suffer of subjugation, killing, and captivity; and in the Hereafter with the punishment of Hell.

In placing the hypocrites before the polytheists there is an indication that they are more severely punished than them and more deserving of what Allah promised them.

Then He described the two groups, saying: ﴿those who harbor an evil assumption about Allah﴾ — which is their assumption that the Prophet (ﷺ) would be defeated and that the word of disbelief would rise above the word of Islam.

Among what they assumed is what Allah related of them in His saying: ﴿Rather you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families again﴾ [al-Fath 48:12]. ﴿Upon them is a circle of evil﴾ — that is, what they assume and wait for against the believers turns back upon them and encircles them. The meaning: the punishment and destruction they expect for the believers fall upon them and descend on them.

Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: "al-Su'" here means corruption. The majority read al-Sau' with a fatha on the sin; Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read it with a damma.

﴿And Allah is angry with them, and has cursed them, and prepared for them Hell, and evil is it as a destination﴾ — when He, glory be to Him, had shown that the circle of evil is upon them in this world, He showed what they deserve besides that: anger, curse, and the punishment of Hell.

﴿And to Allah belong the armies of the heavens and the earth﴾ — of angels, mankind, jinn, and devils. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing, Wise﴾ — He repeated this verse for emphasis. It has been said: what is meant by "armies" here is the armies of punishment, as indicated by the mention of "Mighty" here in place of "Knowing" there.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Mujammi' ibn Harithah al-Ansari, who said: "We witnessed al-Hudaybiyah. When we turned back from it, until we reached Kura' al-Ghamim, the people were urging on their camels. The people said to one another: 'What is the matter with the people?' They said: 'Revelation has come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' So we went out with the people, urging on, and there was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on his riding beast at Kura' al-Ghamim. The people gathered around him, and he recited to them: ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory﴾. A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is it a victory?' He said: 'Yes, by Him in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, it is indeed a victory.' Then Khaybar was divided among the people of al-Hudaybiyah; no one entered with them except those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided it into eighteen shares, and the army was fifteen hundred, including three hundred horsemen; he gave the horseman two shares and the foot soldier one share."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Bukhari in his *Tarikh* (History), Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Dala'il* (Evidences of Prophethood) narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "We were returning from al-Hudaybiyyah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). While we were travelling, revelation came to him. Whenever revelation came to him, it weighed heavily upon him, but then it was lifted from him, and he was filled with such joy as Allah willed. He informed us that it had been revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾."

al-Bukhari and others narrated from Anas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾, that he said: "It is al-Hudaybiyyah."

al-Bukhari and others narrated from al-Bara', who said: "You count the conquest as the conquest of Makkah, and indeed the conquest of Makkah was a conquest. But we count the conquest as the Pledge of al-Ridwan (bay'at al-Ridwan) on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from A'ishah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, regarding ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾: 'It is the conquest of Makkah.'"

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) would pray until his feet swelled. It was said to him: 'Has Allah not forgiven you what came before of your sin and what came after?' He said: 'Should I not be a grateful servant?'" And there are other narrations on this matter.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Dala'il* narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿It is He who sent down tranquility (al-sakinah) into the hearts of the believers﴾, that he said: "Al-sakinah is mercy." And regarding His words ﴿that they may increase in faith along with their faith﴾, he said: "Indeed Allah sent His Prophet (ﷺ) with the testimony that there is no god but Allah (shahadat an la ilaha illa Allah). When the believers affirmed it, He added to them prayer (salah). When they affirmed it, He added to them fasting (sawm). When they affirmed it, He added to them zakah (obligatory charity). When they affirmed it, He added to them the Hajj. When they affirmed it, He added to them jihad."

Then He completed their religion for them, saying: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favour upon you, and approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3].

Ibn Abbas said: "The most firm, the most truthful, and the most complete faith of the people of the heavens and the people of the earth is the testimony that there is no god but Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿that they may increase in faith along with their faith﴾, that he said: "In affirmation along with their affirmation."

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated from Anas, who said: "When the words ﴿that Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾ were revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) on his return from al-Hudaybiyyah, he said: 'Indeed, a verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than everything on earth.' Then he recited it to them. They said: 'Congratulations, O Messenger of Allah! Allah has made clear what He will do with you; but what will He do with us?' Then there was revealed to him: ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally…﴾ until His words ﴿a great achievement﴾."

Others said: it is the Conquest of Khaybar.

It has been said: "Had there been a sin, old or new, We would have forgiven it for you." Other views were stated that have no basis, and the first is the most appropriate.

The meaning of "sin" after prophethood may be the leaving of what is better, and it is called a sin concerning him because of the greatness of his rank, even though it is not a sin in regard to others.

It has been said: it is connected to "yansurak" (aid you): that is, Allah aided you through the believers so that He may admit and punish. He said: 'Yes, by Him in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, it is indeed a victory.' al-Bukhari and others narrated from Anas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾, that he said: "It is al-Hudaybiyyah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from A'ishah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, regarding ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾: 'It is the conquest of Makkah.'"

Ibn Abbas said: "The most firm, the most truthful, and the most complete faith of the people of the heavens and the people of the earth is the testimony that there is no god but Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿that they may increase in faith along with their faith﴾, that he said: "In affirmation along with their affirmation."

Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: "al-Su'" here means corruption. The majority read al-Sau' with a fatha on the sin; Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read it with a damma.

﴿And Allah is angry with them, and has cursed them, and prepared for them Hell, and evil is it as a destination﴾ — when He, glory be to Him, had shown that the circle of evil is upon them in this world, He showed what they deserve besides that: anger, curse, and the punishment of Hell.

﴿And to Allah belong the armies of the heavens and the earth﴾ — of angels, mankind, jinn, and devils. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing, Wise﴾ — He repeated this verse for emphasis. It has been said: what is meant by "armies" here is the armies of punishment, as indicated by the mention of "Mighty" here in place of "Knowing" there.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Mujammi' ibn Harithah al-Ansari, who said: "We witnessed al-Hudaybiyah. When we turned back from it, until we reached Kura' al-Ghamim, the people were urging on their camels. The people said to one another: 'What is the matter with the people?' They said: 'Revelation has come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' So we went out with the people, urging on, and there was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on his riding beast at Kura' al-Ghamim. The people gathered around him, and he recited to them: ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory﴾. A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is it a victory?' He said: 'Yes, by Him in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, it is indeed a victory.' Then Khaybar was divided among the people of al-Hudaybiyah; no one entered with them except those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided it into eighteen shares, and the army was fifteen hundred, including three hundred horsemen; he gave the horseman two shares and the foot soldier one share."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Bukhari in his *Tarikh* (History), Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Dala'il* (Evidences of Prophethood) narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "We were returning from al-Hudaybiyyah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). While we were travelling, revelation came to him. Whenever revelation came to him, it weighed heavily upon him, but then it was lifted from him, and he was filled with such joy as Allah willed. He informed us that it had been revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾."

al-Bukhari and others narrated from Anas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾, that he said: "It is al-Hudaybiyyah."

al-Bukhari and others narrated from al-Bara', who said: "You count the conquest as the conquest of Makkah, and indeed the conquest of Makkah was a conquest. But we count the conquest as the Pledge of al-Ridwan (bay'at al-Ridwan) on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from A'ishah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, regarding ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾: 'It is the conquest of Makkah.'"

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) would pray until his feet swelled. It was said to him: 'Has Allah not forgiven you what came before of your sin and what came after?' He said: 'Should I not be a grateful servant?'" And there are other narrations on this matter.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Dala'il* narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿It is He who sent down tranquility (al-sakinah) into the hearts of the believers﴾, that he said: "Al-sakinah is mercy." And regarding His words ﴿that they may increase in faith along with their faith﴾, he said: "Indeed Allah sent His Prophet (ﷺ) with the testimony that there is no god but Allah (shahadat an la ilaha illa Allah). When the believers affirmed it, He added to them prayer (salah). When they affirmed it, He added to them fasting (sawm). When they affirmed it, He added to them zakah (obligatory charity). When they affirmed it, He added to them the Hajj. When they affirmed it, He added to them jihad."

Then He completed their religion for them, saying: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favour upon you, and approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3].

Ibn Abbas said: "The most firm, the most truthful, and the most complete faith of the people of the heavens and the people of the earth is the testimony that there is no god but Allah."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿that they may increase in faith along with their faith﴾, that he said: "In affirmation along with their affirmation."

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated from Anas, who said: "When the words ﴿that Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾ were revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) on his return from al-Hudaybiyyah, he said: 'Indeed, a verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than everything on earth.' Then he recited it to them. They said: 'Congratulations, O Messenger of Allah! Allah has made clear what He will do with you; but what will He do with us?' Then there was revealed to him: ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally…﴾ until His words ﴿a great achievement﴾."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 48, verses 8–15:

His saying: ﴿Indeed We have sent you as a witness﴾, i.e., over your ummah, by conveying the message to them, and as a bringer of good tidings of Paradise to the obedient, and as a warner to the people of disobedience.

﴿That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾. The majority (al-Jumhur) read "li-tu'minu" with the second person (ta'). Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read it with the third person (ya'). According to the first reading, the address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his ummah; according to the second reading, what is meant is the bearers of good tidings and warners. The accusatives "shahidan," "mubashshiran," and "nadhiran" are in the status of a presumed circumstantial clause (hal muqaddarah). "Wa-tu'azziruhu," "wa-tuwaqqiruhu," and "wa-tusabbihuhu" – the disagreement among the readers regarding these three verbs is like the disagreement regarding "li-tu'minu," as has preceded. The meaning of "tu'azziruhu" is: you magnify him and exalt him, as said by al-Hasan and al-Kalbi. Ta'zir means magnification and veneration.

Qatadah said: you help him and defend him.

'Ikrimah said: you fight alongside him with the sword. The meaning of "tuwaqqiruhu" is: you magnify him.

As-Suddi said: you make him a leader (tusawwiduhu). It has been said: the pronouns in the two verbs refer to the Prophet (ﷺ), and here there is a complete pause (waqf tam), then he begins "wa-tusabbihuhu," i.e., you glorify Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in the morning and evening, i.e., at dawn and at dusk. It has also been said: all the pronouns in the three verbs refer to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so the meaning of "tu'azziruhu" and "tuwaqqiruhu" is: you affirm His oneness and negate partners from Him. It has been said: you help His religion and strive alongside His Messenger.

In "tasbih" there are two meanings: first, declaring Him far exalted above every blemish; second, prayer.

﴿Indeed those who pledge allegiance to you﴾ refers to the Pledge of Good Pleasure (bay'at al-Ridwan) at al-Hudaybiyah, for they pledged under the tree to fight the Quraysh. "They are only pledging to Allah." He, glorified is He, informed that this pledge to His Messenger (ﷺ) is a pledge to Him, as He said: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [an-Nisa: 80]. That is because they sold themselves to Allah for Paradise. The clause ﴿The hand of Allah is over their hands﴾ is a resumptive sentence confirming what precedes, in the manner of imagery (takhyil), in a place of accusative as a circumstantial clause. The meaning is: the contract of the covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is like its contract with Allah, glorified is He, without any difference.

Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is: the blessing of Allah upon them in guidance is above what they did in the pledge.

It has been said: His hand in reward is above their hands in fidelity.

Ibn Kaysan said: the might of Allah and His support are above their might and support. ﴿So whoever breaks [his oath] breaks only against himself﴾, i.e., whoever breaks what he has pledged of the allegiance, then he only breaks against himself, because the harm of that returns to him and does not extend to others. ﴿And whoever fulfills what he has covenanted with Allah﴾, i.e., remains steadfast in fulfilling what he covenanted with Allah in the pledge to His Messenger.

The majority read "'alayhu" with a kasra on the ha'. Hafs and az-Zuhri read it with a damma: ﴿He will give him a great reward﴾, which is Paradise.

The majority read "fasa-yu'tihi" with the third person (ya'). Nafi', Ibn Kathir, and Ibn 'Amir read it with the first person (nun). Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred the first reading, and al-Farra' preferred the second.

﴿The bedouins who were left behind will say to you﴾ are those whom Allah left behind from accompanying His Messenger when he set out in the year of al-Hudaybiyah.

Mujahid and others said: they are the bedouins of Ghifar, Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ashja', and ad-Du'il, who were the bedouins around Madinah.

It has been said: they stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he traveled to Makkah in the year of the Conquest, after he had called them to go out with him. The "mukhallaf" is the one left behind. ﴿Our properties and our families have occupied us﴾, i.e., our wealth, women, and children prevented us from going out with you, and we had no one to take care of them and take our place over them, so ask forgiveness for us that Allah may forgive us what occurred from us of staying behind you for this reason. Since their request for forgiveness was not from belief but in the manner of mockery, and their inner selves opposed their outward appearance, Allah, glorified is He, exposed them with His saying: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾, and this is the practice of the hypocrites. The sentence is a resumptive sentence explaining what their inner selves conceal, and it may be a substitute for the first sentence.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to answer on their behalf, so He said: ﴿Say, "Who then can prevent anything from Allah for you"﴾, i.e., who will hold back what Allah intends for you of good or harm? Then He explained that by saying: ﴿if He intends harm for you﴾, i.e., bringing down what harms you, such as the loss of property and the destruction of families, ﴿or intends for you benefit﴾, i.e., victory and booty.

The majority read "darran" with a fatha on the dad, and it is the verbal noun of "darartuhu darran." Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with a damma, and it is the name of what harms. It has been said: both are dialects. This is a refutation of them when they thought that staying behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would repel harm from them and bring them benefit. Then Allah, glorified is He, turned away from that and said: ﴿Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾, i.e., your staying behind is not for what you claimed; rather Allah was Knowing of all that you do, of which your staying behind is one, and He knew that your staying behind was not for that, but for doubt and hypocrisy and the corrupt suspicions that occurred to you, arising from lack of trust in Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families again﴾. This sentence explains His saying "Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do," because of the vagueness in it: i.e., rather, you thought that the enemy would completely annihilate the believers so that none of them would return to his family, and for that reason you stayed behind, not for the false excuses you mentioned. ﴿And that was made attractive in your hearts﴾, i.e., Satan made that suspicion attractive in your hearts, and you accepted it.

The majority read "wa-zuyyina" in the passive voice; it was also read in the active voice. ﴿And you assumed an assumption of evil﴾, that Allah, glorified is He, would not help His Messenger. This suspicion is either the first suspicion, and the repetition is for emphasis and rebuke, and what is meant by it is more general than the first, so the first suspicion enters under it primarily. ﴿And you were a people deserving of destruction﴾, i.e., ruined. Az-Zajjaj said: ruined before Allah. Mujahid said likewise. Al-Jawhari said: "al-bur" is the corrupt man who is destroyed, in whom there is no good.

Abu 'Ubayd said: "qawman bura" means ruined; it is the plural of ba'ir, like ha'il and hul. "Fulan bara" means he perished, and "abarahu Allah" means Allah destroyed him.

﴿And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger – then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a blaze﴾. This statement is a resumptive sentence from Allah, glorified is He, not included within what Allah commanded His Messenger to say: i.e., whoever does not believe in them, as these stayers-behind did, then his recompense is what Allah has prepared of the torment of the Blaze.

And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He disposes of it as He wills, and He does not need any of His creation. He only imposed worship upon them as He imposed it so that He may reward the one who does good and punish the one who does evil. For this reason He said: ﴿He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wwills﴾ [cf. al-Anbiya: 23: "He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned"]. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful, i.e., abundantly forgiving and merciful, perfect in it, specifying with His forgiveness and mercy whom He wills of His servants.

﴿The ones who were left behind will say, when you set out to take booty, "Leave us that we may follow you."﴾ "Those who were left behind" are those mentioned previously, and the adverbial clause is connected to His saying "will say." The meaning: they will say when you set out, O Muslims, toward booty, i.e., the booty of Khaybar, "that you may take it," i.e., that you may acquire it. "Leave us, we will follow you," i.e., leave us so we may follow you and witness the battle of Khaybar with you.

The origin of the story is that when the Prophet (ﷺ) and those Muslims with him returned from al-Hudaybiyah, Allah promised them the conquest of Khaybar and specified its spoils for those who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyah. When they set out toward it, these stayers-behind said: "Leave us that we may follow you." Then Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿They want to change the words of Allah﴾, i.e., they want to alter the words of Allah. What is meant by these words they wanted to change is the promises of Allah to the people of al-Hudaybiyah specifically regarding the booty of Khaybar.

Muqatil said: it means Allah's command to His Messenger that none of them should march with him.

Ibn Zayd said: it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They ask your permission to go out. Say, "You will never go out with me, and you will never fight with me against an enemy"﴾ [at-Tawbah: 83]. Ibn Jarir and others objected to this, saying that the Expedition of Tabuk was after the conquest of Khaybar and after the conquest of Makkah, and the first is more appropriate. Mujahid and Qatadah said likewise, and Ibn Jarir and others preferred it.

The majority read "kalama Allah," while Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "kalma Allah." Al-Jawhari said: "kalam" is a collective noun applying to few and many, and "kalm" cannot be fewer than three words, because it is the plural of "kalimah," like "naqbah" and "naqb."

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to prevent them from going out with him, so He said: ﴿Say, "You will never follow us. Thus has Allah said before"﴾, i.e., before our return from al-Hudaybiyah, that the booty of Khaybar is for those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyah specifically, and there is no share in it for others. ﴿Then they will say, "Rather, you envy us."﴾ i.e., the hypocrites, upon hearing this statement, which is His saying "You will never follow us." ﴿Rather, what prevents you from going out with us is nothing but envy, lest we share with you in the booty,﴾ and that is not the word of Allah as you claim.

Then Allah, glorified is He, refuted them with His saying: ﴿Rather, they do not understand except a little﴾, i.e., they know only a little knowledge, which is their knowledge of worldly affairs. It has also been said: they understand of the matter of religion only a little understanding, which is what they do in hypocrisy outwardly, not inwardly.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿and you support him﴾ – meaning: the reverence – ﴿and honor him﴾ – meaning: the magnification – meaning Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and adh-Dhiya' in al-Mukhtarah narrated from him regarding His saying "and support him": he said: strike before him with the sword.

Ibn 'Adi, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib, and Ibn 'Asakir in his History narrated from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "When this verse ﴿and support him﴾ was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said to his companions: 'What is that?' They said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'To help him.'"

Ahmad and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: "We pledged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to hear and obey in ease and hardship, in energy and laziness, to spend in hardship and ease, to enjoin good and forbid evil, and that we would speak about Allah without fear of any blame, and that we would support him when he comes to us at Yathrib, and protect him from what we protect ourselves, our wives, and our children, and for us is Paradise. Whoever fulfills it, Allah fulfills for him, and whoever breaks it, then he only breaks against himself."

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Jabir, that they "were at the Pledge of Good Pleasure fifteen hundred," and in the two (Sahihs) from him: that they were fourteen hundred. In al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, that he asked him how many were at the Pledge of Good Pleasure? He said: fifteen hundred. He was told: Jabir said they were fourteen hundred. He said: May Allah have mercy on him; he erred. He narrated to me that they were fifteen hundred.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 48, verses 8–15:

His saying: ﴿Indeed We have sent you as a witness﴾, i.e., over your ummah, by conveying the message to them, and as a bringer of good tidings of Paradise to the obedient, and as a warner to the people of disobedience.

According to the first reading, the address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his ummah; according to the second reading, what is meant is the bearers of good tidings and warners. The accusatives "shahidan," "mubashshiran," and "nadhiran" are in the status of a presumed circumstantial clause (hal muqaddarah). "Wa-tu'azziruhu," "wa-tuwaqqiruhu," and "wa-tusabbihuhu" – the disagreement among the readers regarding these three verbs is like the disagreement regarding "li-tu'minu," as has preceded. The meaning of "tu'azziruhu" is: you magnify him and exalt him, as said by al-Hasan and al-Kalbi. Ta'zir means magnification and veneration.

Qatadah said: you help him and defend him.

'Ikrimah said: you fight alongside him with the sword. The meaning of "tuwaqqiruhu" is: you magnify him.

As-Suddi said: you make him a leader (tusawwiduhu). It has been said: the pronouns in the two verbs refer to the Prophet (ﷺ), and here there is a complete pause (waqf tam), then he begins "wa-tusabbihuhu," i.e., you glorify Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in the morning and evening, i.e., at dawn and at dusk. It has also been said: all the pronouns in the three verbs refer to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so the meaning of "tu'azziruhu" and "tuwaqqiruhu" is: you affirm His oneness and negate partners from Him. It has been said: you help His religion and strive alongside His Messenger.

In "tasbih" there are two meanings: first, declaring Him far exalted above every blemish; second, prayer.

﴿Indeed those who pledge allegiance to you﴾ refers to the Pledge of Good Pleasure (bay'at al-Ridwan) at al-Hudaybiyah, for they pledged under the tree to fight the Quraysh. "They are only pledging to Allah." He, glorified is He, informed that this pledge to His Messenger (ﷺ) is a pledge to Him, as He said: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [an-Nisa: 80]. That is because they sold themselves to Allah for Paradise. The clause ﴿The hand of Allah is over their hands﴾ is a resumptive sentence confirming what precedes, in the manner of imagery (takhyil), in a place of accusative as a circumstantial clause. The meaning is: the contract of the covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is like its contract with Allah, glorified is He, without any difference.

Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is: the blessing of Allah upon them in guidance is above what they did in the pledge.

It has been said: His hand in reward is above their hands in fidelity.

Ibn Kaysan said: the might of Allah and His support are above their might and support. ﴿So whoever breaks [his oath] breaks only against himself﴾, i.e., whoever breaks what he has pledged of the allegiance, then he only breaks against himself, because the harm of that returns to him and does not extend to others. ﴿And whoever fulfills what he has covenanted with Allah﴾, i.e., remains steadfast in fulfilling what he covenanted with Allah in the pledge to His Messenger.

The majority read "'alayhu" with a kasra on the ha'. Hafs and az-Zuhri read it with a damma: ﴿He will give him a great reward﴾, which is Paradise.

The majority read "fasa-yu'tihi" with the third person (ya'). Nafi', Ibn Kathir, and Ibn 'Amir read it with the first person (nun). Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred the first reading, and al-Farra' preferred the second.

﴿The bedouins who were left behind will say to you﴾ are those whom Allah left behind from accompanying His Messenger when he set out in the year of al-Hudaybiyah.

Mujahid and others said: they are the bedouins of Ghifar, Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ashja', and ad-Du'il, who were the bedouins around Madinah.

It has been said: they stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he traveled to Makkah in the year of the Conquest, after he had called them to go out with him. The "mukhallaf" is the one left behind. ﴿Our properties and our families have occupied us﴾, i.e., our wealth, women, and children prevented us from going out with you, and we had no one to take care of them and take our place over them, so ask forgiveness for us that Allah may forgive us what occurred from us of staying behind you for this reason. Since their request for forgiveness was not from belief but in the manner of mockery, and their inner selves opposed their outward appearance, Allah, glorified is He, exposed them with His saying: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾, and this is the practice of the hypocrites. The sentence is a resumptive sentence explaining what their inner selves conceal, and it may be a substitute for the first sentence.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to answer on their behalf, so He said: ﴿Say, "Who then can prevent anything from Allah for you"﴾, i.e., who will hold back what Allah intends for you of good or harm? Then He explained that by saying: ﴿if He intends harm for you﴾, i.e., bringing down what harms you, such as the loss of property and the destruction of families, ﴿or intends for you benefit﴾, i.e., victory and booty.

The majority read "darran" with a fatha on the dad, and it is the verbal noun of "darartuhu darran." Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with a damma, and it is the name of what harms. It has been said: both are dialects. This is a refutation of them when they thought that staying behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would repel harm from them and bring them benefit. Then Allah, glorified is He, turned away from that and said: ﴿Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾, i.e., your staying behind is not for what you claimed; rather Allah was Knowing of all that you do, of which your staying behind is one, and He knew that your staying behind was not for that, but for doubt and hypocrisy and the corrupt suspicions that occurred to you, arising from lack of trust in Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families again﴾. This sentence explains His saying "Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do," because of the vagueness in it: i.e., rather, you thought that the enemy would completely annihilate the believers so that none of them would return to his family, and for that reason you stayed behind, not for the false excuses you mentioned. ﴿And that was made attractive in your hearts﴾, i.e., Satan made that suspicion attractive in your hearts, and you accepted it.

The majority read "wa-zuyyina" in the passive voice; it was also read in the active voice. ﴿And you assumed an assumption of evil﴾, that Allah, glorified is He, would not help His Messenger. This suspicion is either the first suspicion, and the repetition is for emphasis and rebuke, and what is meant by it is more general than the first, so the first suspicion enters under it primarily. ﴿And you were a people deserving of destruction﴾, i.e., ruined. Az-Zajjaj said: ruined before Allah. Mujahid said likewise. Al-Jawhari said: "al-bur" is the corrupt man who is destroyed, in whom there is no good.

Abu 'Ubayd said: "qawman bura" means ruined; it is the plural of ba'ir, like ha'il and hul. "Fulan bara" means he perished, and "abarahu Allah" means Allah destroyed him.

He only imposed worship upon them as He imposed it so that He may reward the one who does good and punish the one who does evil. According to the first reading, the address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his ummah; according to the second reading, what is meant is the bearers of good tidings and warners. The accusatives "shahidan," "mubashshiran," and "nadhiran" are in the status of a presumed circumstantial clause (hal muqaddarah). The meaning of "tu'azziruhu" is: you magnify him and exalt him, as said by al-Hasan and al-Kalbi. Ta'zir means magnification and veneration.

Qatadah said: you help him and defend him.

'Ikrimah said: you fight alongside him with the sword. The meaning of "tuwaqqiruhu" is: you magnify him.

As-Suddi said: you make him a leader (tusawwiduhu). It has been said: the pronouns in the two verbs refer to the Prophet (ﷺ), and here there is a complete pause (waqf tam), then he begins "wa-tusabbihuhu," i.e., you glorify Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in the morning and evening, i.e., at dawn and at dusk. It has also been said: all the pronouns in the three verbs refer to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so the meaning of "tu'azziruhu" and "tuwaqqiruhu" is: you affirm His oneness and negate partners from Him. It has been said: you help His religion and strive alongside His Messenger.

In "tasbih" there are two meanings: first, declaring Him far exalted above every blemish; second, prayer.

﴿Indeed those who pledge allegiance to you﴾ refers to the Pledge of Good Pleasure (bay'at al-Ridwan) at al-Hudaybiyah, for they pledged under the tree to fight the Quraysh. "They are only pledging to Allah." He, glorified is He, informed that this pledge to His Messenger (ﷺ) is a pledge to Him, as He said: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [an-Nisa: 80]. That is because they sold themselves to Allah for Paradise. The clause ﴿The hand of Allah is over their hands﴾ is a resumptive sentence confirming what precedes, in the manner of imagery (takhyil), in a place of accusative as a circumstantial clause. The meaning is: the contract of the covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is like its contract with Allah, glorified is He, without any difference.

Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is: the blessing of Allah upon them in guidance is above what they did in the pledge.

It has been said: His hand in reward is above their hands in fidelity.

Ibn Kaysan said: the might of Allah and His support are above their might and support. ﴿So whoever breaks [his oath] breaks only against himself﴾, i.e., whoever breaks what he has pledged of the allegiance, then he only breaks against himself, because the harm of that returns to him and does not extend to others. ﴿And whoever fulfills what he has covenanted with Allah﴾, i.e., remains steadfast in fulfilling what he covenanted with Allah in the pledge to His Messenger.

The majority read "'alayhu" with a kasra on the ha'. Hafs and az-Zuhri read it with a damma: ﴿He will give him a great reward﴾, which is Paradise.

The majority read "fasa-yu'tihi" with the third person (ya'). Nafi', Ibn Kathir, and Ibn 'Amir read it with the first person (nun). Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred the first reading, and al-Farra' preferred the second.

﴿The bedouins who were left behind will say to you﴾ are those whom Allah left behind from accompanying His Messenger when he set out in the year of al-Hudaybiyah.

Mujahid and others said: they are the bedouins of Ghifar, Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ashja', and ad-Du'il, who were the bedouins around Madinah.

It has been said: they stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he traveled to Makkah in the year of the Conquest, after he had called them to go out with him. The "mukhallaf" is the one left behind. ﴿Our properties and our families have occupied us﴾, i.e., our wealth, women, and children prevented us from going out with you, and we had no one to take care of them and take our place over them, so ask forgiveness for us that Allah may forgive us what occurred from us of staying behind you for this reason. Since their request for forgiveness was not from belief but in the manner of mockery, and their inner selves opposed their outward appearance, Allah, glorified is He, exposed them with His saying: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾, and this is the practice of the hypocrites. The sentence is a resumptive sentence explaining what their inner selves conceal, and it may be a substitute for the first sentence.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to answer on their behalf, so He said: ﴿Say, "Who then can prevent anything from Allah for you"﴾, i.e., who will hold back what Allah intends for you of good or harm? Then He explained that by saying: ﴿if He intends harm for you﴾, i.e., bringing down what harms you, such as the loss of property and the destruction of families, ﴿or intends for you benefit﴾, i.e., victory and booty.

The majority read "darran" with a fatha on the dad, and it is the verbal noun of "darartuhu darran." Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with a damma, and it is the name of what harms. It has been said: both are dialects. This is a refutation of them when they thought that staying behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would repel harm from them and bring them benefit. Then Allah, glorified is He, turned away from that and said: ﴿Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾, i.e., your staying behind is not for what you claimed; rather Allah was Knowing of all that you do, of which your staying behind is one, and He knew that your staying behind was not for that, but for doubt and hypocrisy and the corrupt suspicions that occurred to you, arising from lack of trust in Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families again﴾. This sentence explains His saying "Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do," because of the vagueness in it: i.e., rather, you thought that the enemy would completely annihilate the believers so that none of them would return to his family, and for that reason you stayed behind, not for the false excuses you mentioned. ﴿And that was made attractive in your hearts﴾, i.e., Satan made that suspicion attractive in your hearts, and you accepted it.

The majority read "wa-zuyyina" in the passive voice; it was also read in the active voice. ﴿And you assumed an assumption of evil﴾, that Allah, glorified is He, would not help His Messenger. This suspicion is either the first suspicion, and the repetition is for emphasis and rebuke, and what is meant by it is more general than the first, so the first suspicion enters under it primarily. ﴿And you were a people deserving of destruction﴾, i.e., ruined. Az-Zajjaj said: ruined before Allah. Mujahid said likewise. Al-Jawhari said: "al-bur" is the corrupt man who is destroyed, in whom there is no good.

Abu 'Ubayd said: "qawman bura" means ruined; it is the plural of ba'ir, like ha'il and hul. "Fulan bara" means he perished, and "abarahu Allah" means Allah destroyed him.

He only imposed worship upon them as He imposed it so that He may reward the one who does good and punish the one who does evil. He was told: Jabir said they were fourteen hundred. He said: May Allah have mercy on him; he erred. He narrated to me that they were fifteen hundred.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 48, verses 8–15:

His saying: ﴿Indeed We have sent you as a witness﴾, i.e., over your ummah, by conveying the message to them, and as a bringer of good tidings of Paradise to the obedient, and as a warner to the people of disobedience.

﴿That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾. The majority (al-Jumhur) read "li-tu'minu" with the second person (ta'). Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read it with the third person (ya'). According to the first reading, the address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his ummah; according to the second reading, what is meant is the bearers of good tidings and warners. The accusatives "shahidan," "mubashshiran," and "nadhiran" are in the status of a presumed circumstantial clause (hal muqaddarah). "Wa-tu'azziruhu," "wa-tuwaqqiruhu," and "wa-tusabbihuhu" – the disagreement among the readers regarding these three verbs is like the disagreement regarding "li-tu'minu," as has preceded. The meaning of "tu'azziruhu" is: you magnify him and exalt him, as said by al-Hasan and al-Kalbi. Ta'zir means magnification and veneration.

Qatadah said: you help him and defend him.

'Ikrimah said: you fight alongside him with the sword. The meaning of "tuwaqqiruhu" is: you magnify him.

As-Suddi said: you make him a leader (tusawwiduhu). It has been said: the pronouns in the two verbs refer to the Prophet (ﷺ), and here there is a complete pause (waqf tam), then he begins "wa-tusabbihuhu," i.e., you glorify Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in the morning and evening, i.e., at dawn and at dusk. It has also been said: all the pronouns in the three verbs refer to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so the meaning of "tu'azziruhu" and "tuwaqqiruhu" is: you affirm His oneness and negate partners from Him. It has been said: you help His religion and strive alongside His Messenger.

In "tasbih" there are two meanings: first, declaring Him far exalted above every blemish; second, prayer.

﴿Indeed those who pledge allegiance to you﴾ refers to the Pledge of Good Pleasure (bay'at al-Ridwan) at al-Hudaybiyah, for they pledged under the tree to fight the Quraysh. "They are only pledging to Allah." He, glorified is He, informed that this pledge to His Messenger (ﷺ) is a pledge to Him, as He said: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [an-Nisa: 80]. That is because they sold themselves to Allah for Paradise. The clause ﴿The hand of Allah is over their hands﴾ is a resumptive sentence confirming what precedes, in the manner of imagery (takhyil), in a place of accusative as a circumstantial clause. The meaning is: the contract of the covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is like its contract with Allah, glorified is He, without any difference.

Al-Kalbi said: the meaning is: the blessing of Allah upon them in guidance is above what they did in the pledge.

It has been said: His hand in reward is above their hands in fidelity.

Ibn Kaysan said: the might of Allah and His support are above their might and support. ﴿So whoever breaks [his oath] breaks only against himself﴾, i.e., whoever breaks what he has pledged of the allegiance, then he only breaks against himself, because the harm of that returns to him and does not extend to others. ﴿And whoever fulfills what he has covenanted with Allah﴾, i.e., remains steadfast in fulfilling what he covenanted with Allah in the pledge to His Messenger.

The majority read "'alayhu" with a kasra on the ha'. Hafs and az-Zuhri read it with a damma: ﴿He will give him a great reward﴾, which is Paradise.

The majority read "fasa-yu'tihi" with the third person (ya'). Nafi', Ibn Kathir, and Ibn 'Amir read it with the first person (nun). Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred the first reading, and al-Farra' preferred the second.

﴿The bedouins who were left behind will say to you﴾ are those whom Allah left behind from accompanying His Messenger when he set out in the year of al-Hudaybiyah.

Mujahid and others said: they are the bedouins of Ghifar, Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ashja', and ad-Du'il, who were the bedouins around Madinah.

It has been said: they stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he traveled to Makkah in the year of the Conquest, after he had called them to go out with him. The "mukhallaf" is the one left behind. ﴿Our properties and our families have occupied us﴾, i.e., our wealth, women, and children prevented us from going out with you, and we had no one to take care of them and take our place over them, so ask forgiveness for us that Allah may forgive us what occurred from us of staying behind you for this reason. Since their request for forgiveness was not from belief but in the manner of mockery, and their inner selves opposed their outward appearance, Allah, glorified is He, exposed them with His saying: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾, and this is the practice of the hypocrites. The sentence is a resumptive sentence explaining what their inner selves conceal, and it may be a substitute for the first sentence.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to answer on their behalf, so He said: ﴿Say, "Who then can prevent anything from Allah for you"﴾, i.e., who will hold back what Allah intends for you of good or harm? Then He explained that by saying: ﴿if He intends harm for you﴾, i.e., bringing down what harms you, such as the loss of property and the destruction of families, ﴿or intends for you benefit﴾, i.e., victory and booty.

The majority read "darran" with a fatha on the dad, and it is the verbal noun of "darartuhu darran." Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with a damma, and it is the name of what harms. It has been said: both are dialects. This is a refutation of them when they thought that staying behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would repel harm from them and bring them benefit. Then Allah, glorified is He, turned away from that and said: ﴿Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾, i.e., your staying behind is not for what you claimed; rather Allah was Knowing of all that you do, of which your staying behind is one, and He knew that your staying behind was not for that, but for doubt and hypocrisy and the corrupt suspicions that occurred to you, arising from lack of trust in Allah. For this reason He said: ﴿Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families again﴾. This sentence explains His saying "Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do," because of the vagueness in it: i.e., rather, you thought that the enemy would completely annihilate the believers so that none of them would return to his family, and for that reason you stayed behind, not for the false excuses you mentioned. ﴿And that was made attractive in your hearts﴾, i.e., Satan made that suspicion attractive in your hearts, and you accepted it.

The majority read "wa-zuyyina" in the passive voice; it was also read in the active voice. ﴿And you assumed an assumption of evil﴾, that Allah, glorified is He, would not help His Messenger. This suspicion is either the first suspicion, and the repetition is for emphasis and rebuke, and what is meant by it is more general than the first, so the first suspicion enters under it primarily. ﴿And you were a people deserving of destruction﴾, i.e., ruined. Az-Zajjaj said: ruined before Allah. Mujahid said likewise. Al-Jawhari said: "al-bur" is the corrupt man who is destroyed, in whom there is no good.

Abu 'Ubayd said: "qawman bura" means ruined; it is the plural of ba'ir, like ha'il and hul. "Fulan bara" means he perished, and "abarahu Allah" means Allah destroyed him.

﴿And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger – then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a blaze﴾. This statement is a resumptive sentence from Allah, glorified is He, not included within what Allah commanded His Messenger to say: i.e., whoever does not believe in them, as these stayers-behind did, then his recompense is what Allah has prepared of the torment of the Blaze.

And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He disposes of it as He wills, and He does not need any of His creation. He only imposed worship upon them as He imposed it so that He may reward the one who does good and punish the one who does evil. For this reason He said: ﴿He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wwills﴾ [cf. al-Anbiya: 23: "He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned"]. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful, i.e., abundantly forgiving and merciful, perfect in it, specifying with His forgiveness and mercy whom He wills of His servants.

﴿The ones who were left behind will say, when you set out to take booty, "Leave us that we may follow you."﴾ "Those who were left behind" are those mentioned previously, and the adverbial clause is connected to His saying "will say." The meaning: they will say when you set out, O Muslims, toward booty, i.e., the booty of Khaybar, "that you may take it," i.e., that you may acquire it. "Leave us, we will follow you," i.e., leave us so we may follow you and witness the battle of Khaybar with you.

The origin of the story is that when the Prophet (ﷺ) and those Muslims with him returned from al-Hudaybiyah, Allah promised them the conquest of Khaybar and specified its spoils for those who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyah. When they set out toward it, these stayers-behind said: "Leave us that we may follow you." Then Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿They want to change the words of Allah﴾, i.e., they want to alter the words of Allah. What is meant by these words they wanted to change is the promises of Allah to the people of al-Hudaybiyah specifically regarding the booty of Khaybar.

Muqatil said: it means Allah's command to His Messenger that none of them should march with him.

Ibn Zayd said: it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They ask your permission to go out. Say, "You will never go out with me, and you will never fight with me against an enemy"﴾ [at-Tawbah: 83]. Ibn Jarir and others objected to this, saying that the Expedition of Tabuk was after the conquest of Khaybar and after the conquest of Makkah, and the first is more appropriate. Mujahid and Qatadah said likewise, and Ibn Jarir and others preferred it.

The majority read "kalama Allah," while Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "kalma Allah." Al-Jawhari said: "kalam" is a collective noun applying to few and many, and "kalm" cannot be fewer than three words, because it is the plural of "kalimah," like "naqbah" and "naqb."

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to prevent them from going out with him, so He said: ﴿Say, "You will never follow us. Thus has Allah said before"﴾, i.e., before our return from al-Hudaybiyah, that the booty of Khaybar is for those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyah specifically, and there is no share in it for others. ﴿Then they will say, "Rather, you envy us."﴾ i.e., the hypocrites, upon hearing this statement, which is His saying "You will never follow us." ﴿Rather, what prevents you from going out with us is nothing but envy, lest we share with you in the booty,﴾ and that is not the word of Allah as you claim.

Then Allah, glorified is He, refuted them with His saying: ﴿Rather, they do not understand except a little﴾, i.e., they know only a little knowledge, which is their knowledge of worldly affairs. It has also been said: they understand of the matter of religion only a little understanding, which is what they do in hypocrisy outwardly, not inwardly.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿and you support him﴾ – meaning: the reverence – ﴿and honor him﴾ – meaning: the magnification – meaning Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and adh-Dhiya' in al-Mukhtarah narrated from him regarding His saying "and support him": he said: strike before him with the sword.

Ibn 'Adi, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Khatib, and Ibn 'Asakir in his History narrated from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "When this verse ﴿and support him﴾ was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said to his companions: 'What is that?' They said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'To help him.'"

Whoever fulfills it, Allah fulfills for him, and whoever breaks it, then he only breaks against himself."

He was told: Jabir said they were fourteen hundred. He said: May Allah have mercy on him; he erred. He narrated to me that they were fifteen hundred.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 48, verse 16–24 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿Say to the desert Arabs who were left behind﴾: they are those mentioned earlier. This is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Allah was well pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree﴾. Then he pledged allegiance for ʿUthman with one of his hands upon the other, and the people said: 'Congratulations to Ibn ʿAffān, he circumambulates the House while we are here.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Even if he remained such-and-such years, he would not circumambulate until I circumambulate.'"

Ibn Abi Shayba in al-Muṣannaf related from Nafiʿ who said: "It reached ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that people were going to the tree under which the pledge had been taken, so he ordered it to be cut down."

Muslim and others related from Jabir who said: "We pledged to him that we would not flee, and we did not pledge to him upon death."

Ibn Mardawayh also related from him regarding (﴿So He hastened this for you﴾) that it means Khaybar, (﴿and restrained the hands of the people from you﴾) meaning the people of Mecca, from desecrating the sanctuary of Allah while you were in the state of ihram.

It is also narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said: they are Persia and the Byzantines.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: they are Hawazin and Thaqif.

ʿIkrima said: Hawazin.

Qatada said: Hawazin and Ghatafan on the day of Ḥunayn.

al-Zuhrī and Muqatil said: they are Banu Ḥanifa, the people of al-Yamama, the companions of Musaylima.

(﴿But if you turn away﴾), that is, you refuse, (﴿as you turned away before﴾), referring to the year of al-Ḥudaybiyya, (﴿He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾), by killing, capture, and subjugation in this world, and by the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter, because your sin is doubled.

﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick﴾: that is, there is no blame upon these excused people for remaining behind from the campaign, because they are unable.

Muqatil said: Allah excused the disabled people who stayed behind from marching to al-Ḥudaybiyya by this verse. The word ḥaraj (blame) means sin. al-Farrāʾ said: that is, He knew what was in their hearts of truthfulness and loyalty.

Qatada and Ibn Jurayj said: of contentment with the matter of the pledge, that they would not flee.

Muqatil said: of reluctance toward the pledge upon death. (﴿So He sent down tranquility upon them﴾) is conjoined to (raḍiya, "was pleased"). Al-sakīna is tranquility and calmness of the soul, as has been mentioned earlier. It is said: it is patience. This was said by Qatada, Ibn Abi Layla, and others. It is also said: it is the conquest of Mecca, but the first is preferable.

﴿And abundant spoils that they will take﴾: that is, and He rewarded you with abundant spoils, or He gave them to you, and these were the spoils of Khaybar. The shift to direct address is to honour them. ﴿And Allah is ever Mighty and Wise﴾: that is, Victorious, executing His actions and words in the manner of wisdom.

﴿Allah has promised you abundant spoils that you will take﴾: in this is a promise from Him, glorified is He, to His believing servants of what He will open for them of spoils until the Day of Resurrection, which they will take at the times decreed for their occurrence. It is also said: the treaty of al-Ḥudaybiyya. ﴿And He restrained the hands of the people from you﴾: that is, He restrained the hands of the Quraysh from you on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyya by the treaty. It is also said: He restrained the hands of the people of Khaybar and their allies from fighting you, and He cast terror into their hearts.

Qatada said: He restrained the hands of the Jews from Medina after the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to al-Ḥudaybiyya and Khaybar. al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Abi Ishaq said: it is Khaybar, which Allah promised to His Prophet before he conquered it, and they had not been expecting it.

And Allah is over all things Competent, His power is not limited to some of the things that can be done over others.

﴿And if those who disbelieved had fought you, they would have turned their backs﴾: Qatada said this refers to the disbelievers of Quraysh at al-Ḥudaybiyya. It is also said: Asad and Ghatafan, who intended to help the people of Khaybar. The first is preferable. Then they would not find a guardian to support them against you, nor a helper to aid them against you.

The accusative of (sunnata, "way") is as a verbal noun with an omitted verb: that is, Allah established the way of Allah; or it is a verbal noun emphasizing the content of the preceding sentence. (﴿You will not find for the way of Allah any change﴾): that is, you will not find any alteration in it, rather it is continuous and established.

﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them within Mecca after He had given you victory over them﴾: that is, He restrained the hands of the polytheists from the Muslims and the hands of the Muslims from the polytheists when they came to prevent the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and those with him from the House in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyya; and this is what is meant by "within Mecca" (baṭn Makka). It is said that eighty men from the people of Mecca descended upon the Prophet (ﷺ) from the direction of the mountain of al-Tanʿīm, armed, intending to surprise the Prophet (ﷺ), but the Muslims seized them, then released them.

There is a difference in the narration which will be explained at the end of the discussion, God willing. And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do, nothing of that is hidden from Him.

ʿIkrima said: Hawazin.

Qatada said: Hawazin and Ghatafan on the day of Ḥunayn.

al-Zuhrī and Muqatil said: they are Banu Ḥanifa, the people of al-Yamama, the companions of Musaylima.

al-Wahidi related this view from most of the commentators. (﴿You will fight them, or they will submit﴾) That is, one of two things will occur: either fighting or Islam, with no third alternative. This is the ruling for the disbelievers from whom the jizya (poll tax) is not taken.

al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is "or they submit" (aw hum yuslimun). In the recitation of Ubayy it is (aw yuslimū), meaning: "until they submit." (﴿If you obey, Allah will give you a good reward﴾), which is booty in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter. (﴿But if you turn away﴾), that is, you refuse, (﴿as you turned away before﴾), referring to the year of al-Ḥudaybiyya, (﴿He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾), by killing, capture, and subjugation in this world, and by the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter, because your sin is doubled.

﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick﴾: that is, there is no blame upon these excused people for remaining behind from the campaign, because they are unable.

Muqatil said: Allah excused the disabled people who stayed behind from marching to al-Ḥudaybiyya by this verse. The word ḥaraj (blame) means sin. This tree mentioned was a tree that existed at al-Ḥudaybiyya; it is said it was a lote tree (sidra). The pledge was to fight the Quraysh and not to flee.

It is narrated that he took the pledge upon death, and the number of those who took this pledge was mentioned shortly before; the account is detailed in the books of ḥadīth and biography. (﴿He knew what was in their hearts﴾) is conjoined to (yubāyiʿūnaka).

Qatada and Ibn Jurayj said: of contentment with the matter of the pledge, that they would not flee.

(p-1386) His words: "They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque" — meaning the disbelievers of Makkah. The meaning of their barring you from the Sacred Mosque is that they prevented you from circumambulating it and from being released from your ʿumrah (pilgrimage), and "the offering (al-hady) detained (maʿkūfan)." The majority (al-Jumhūr) read "al-hadya" in the accusative, as a conjunction with the object pronoun in "ṣaddūkum." Abū ʿAmr, in one narration from him, read it in the genitive, as a conjunction with "al-Masjid," and a governing noun must be supplied: i.e., "from the slaughtering of the offering." It was also read in the nominative, on the assumption: "and the offering was barred." The majority read the ha' of "al-hady" with a fatha and the dal with a sukun; it is narrated from Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim that the dal has a kasra and the yā' is shaddah. The accusative of "maʿkūfan" is a circumstantial state (ḥāl) of "al-hady," meaning: held back.

Al-Jawharī said: "ʿakafahu" means he held him back and stopped him; from this comes "wal-hadya maʿkūfan," and from this comes "al-iʿtikāf" in the mosque, which is confinement.

Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "maʿkūfan" means gathered together.

His words: "an yablugha maḥillahu" — i.e., "from reaching its place of sacrifice," or it is a object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), and the meaning is: "they barred the offering out of dislike that it reach its place of sacrifice." Or it is a substitute for "al-hady" as a substitution of inclusion (badal ishtimāl). "Maḥillahu" means its place of slaughter, which is where its slaughter is permitted within the Ḥaram. The offering was seventy camels, and Allah, glorified is He, granted them dispensation to make that place, which they had reached — al-Ḥudaybiyah — a place of sacrifice. There is a well-known discussion among the scholars on this in the books of jurisprudence (furūʿ).

"And had there not been believing men and believing women whom you did not know" — meaning the oppressed believers in Makkah. The meaning of "lam taʿlamūhum" is "you did not recognize them." It was said: "you did not know that they were believers, lest you trample them." It may be a substitute for "rijāl" and "nisāʾ," but the masculine was given precedence. It may also be a substitute for the object of "taʿlamūhum," and the meaning is: "lest you trample them" by killing and striking them. It is said: "wataʾtu al-qawm," meaning I struck the people. That is because, if they had conquered Makkah and taken it by force with the sword, the believers who were there would not have been distinguished from the disbelievers, and at that point they would not be safe from killing the believers, so that expiation (kaffārah) would become obligatory for them and disgrace would befall them. This is the meaning of His words: "then there would befall you from them" — that is, from their direction — "maʿarrah," meaning hardship, through what would be obligatory upon them in killing them of expiation and blame. The root of maʿarrah is blame, taken from ʿurr, which is mange. That is because the polytheists would say: "The Muslims have killed the people of their own religion."

Al-Zajjaj said: "Lawlā an taqtulū rijālan mu'minīna wa nisā'an mu'mināti fa-tuṣībakum minhum maʿarratun" — i.e., sin.

Likewise said al-Jawharī, and Ibn Zayd said similarly.

Al-Kalbī, Muqātil and others said: maʿarrah is the expiation for accidental killing, as in His words: "And if he was from a people hostile to you and he was a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave" [al-Nisāʾ: 92]. Ibn Isḥāq said: maʿarrah is the payment of blood money (diyah).

Quṭrub said: maʿarrah is hardship. It was also said: distress.

"Bi-ghayri ʿilm" is connected to "an taṭaʾūhum": i.e., without knowing. The answer to "lawlā" is omitted, and the estimate is: "Allah would have permitted you" or "He would have restrained your hands from them." The lām in "li-yudkhila Allāhu fī raḥmatihi man yashāʾ" is connected to what the omitted answer indicates: i.e., "but He did not permit you," or "He restrained your hands so that Allah might admit into His mercy whom He wills from His servants, namely the believing men and believing women who were in Makkah." Thus He would complete their rewards by bringing them out from among the disbelievers, free their captivity, and remove the punishment that was descending upon them.

It was also said: the lām is connected to an omitted element other than what has been mentioned, and its estimate is: "Had you killed them, Allah would have admitted them into His mercy." The first is preferable.

It was also said: "whom He wills" refers to His servants from among the polytheists who had inclined to Islam. "Had they been distinguished, We would have punished those among them who disbelieved with a painful punishment." Tazayyul means distinction, i.e., had those who believed been distinguished from those who disbelieved among them, We would have punished those who disbelieved. It was also said: tazayyul means separation, i.e., had these been separated from those. It was said: had the believers departed from among them. The meanings are close. The painful punishment is killing, captivity, and subjugation.

The adverbial clause in His words "idh jaʿala alladhīna kafarū" is governed by an omitted verb: i.e., "remember the time when those who disbelieved placed." It was said: it is connected to "ʿaḏḏabnā." Ḥamiyyah means haughtiness. It is said: "Fulān dhū ḥamiyyah," i.e., he has haughtiness and anger. That is, they made it firmly established in their hearts. The "jaʿl" here means placing, and "ḥamiyyat al-jāhiliyyah" is an appositive substitute for "al-ḥamiyyah."

Muqātil ibn Sulaymān and Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said: the people of Makkah said: "They have killed our sons and brothers, and they enter upon us in our homes, so the Arabs will say that they entered upon us in spite of our noses. By al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, they will not enter it upon us." This is the ḥamiyyat al-jāhiliyyah which entered their hearts.

al-Zuhrī said: their ḥamiyyah was their refusal to acknowledge the Prophet (ﷺ) as a messenger.

The majority read "law tazayyalū." Ibn Abī ʿAbla, Abū Ḥaywah and Ibn ʿAwn read "law tazāyalū," and tazāyul means separation.

"Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers" — i.e., He sent down calm and dignity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, since the ḥamiyyah that entered the people of disbelief did not enter them. It was said: He made them firm in contentment and submission.

"And He made them adhere to the word of piety" — which is "There is no god but Allah." This is what the majority said, and some added: "Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah," and some added: "alone, with no partner."

al-Zuhrī said: it is "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful," because the disbelievers did not acknowledge it and refused to write it in the treaty of peace that was between them and the Messenger of Allah (p-1387) (ﷺ), as is established in the books of ḥadīth and sīrah. So Allah specified this word for the believers and made them adhere to it. The first is preferable, because the word of tawḥīd is that by which polytheism against Allah is guarded against. It was said: the word of piety is fulfilling the covenant and steadfastness upon it.

"And they were more deserving of it and worthy of it" — i.e., the believers were more deserving of this word than the disbelievers, and more fit for it than they, because Allah, glorified is He, qualified them for His religion and for companionship with His Messenger (ﷺ).

"Indeed Allah fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth."
